findings.title: Type safety: any-typed array in analytics
findings.description: In googleAnalyticsUtils.ts, an array is typed as `any[]` which bypasses TypeScript's type checking and can lead to runtime errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Define a proper interface for the referrer data type: `interface ReferrerData { source: string; visitors: string; }` and use `ReferrerData[]` instead of `any[]`.

findings.title: Type safety: @ts-ignore usage in analytics
findings.description: Multiple `@ts-ignore` comments are used to suppress TypeScript errors, indicating underlying type issues that should be properly resolved.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove @ts-ignore comments and properly type the response objects. The `response.rows` and `metricValues` properties should have proper types from the Google Analytics Data client.

findings.title: Magic number: URL expiration timeout repeated across files
findings.description: The value 3600 (seconds) for signed URL expiration is hardcoded in multiple files. This should be a named constant.
findings.suggested_fix: Create a constants file (e.g., `src/shared/constants.ts`) with `export const SIGNED_URL_EXPIRATION_SECONDS = 3600;` and import it in both files.

findings.title: Magic number: Hardcoded redirect delay in CheckoutResultPage
findings.description: The redirect delay value 4000ms is hardcoded and used both as a constant and inline in the code, creating potential inconsistency.
findings.suggested_fix: The constant is properly defined and used, but this pattern should be consistent across all timing-related values. Consider moving all timing constants to a shared location.

findings.title: Code duplication: Duplicate headers object in Plausible analytics
findings.description: A `headers` object with identical content is defined both at module level and within the `getPageviewsForDate` function, creating redundant code.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the local `headers` variable inside `getPageviewsForDate` and use the module-level `headers` constant directly, or pass it as a parameter if it needs to be reused differently.

findings.title: Inconsistent naming: Mixed camelCase and snake_case in analytics
findings.description: Some functions use camelCase (getDailyPageViews) while others use similar patterns inconsistently. The API keys are also named with inconsistent patterns (PLAUSIBLE_API_KEY vs GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_PROPERTY_ID).
findings.suggested_fix: Document the environment variable naming convention and ensure consistency. Consider creating a unified env config file that normalizes all environment variable access.

findings.title: Potential runtime error: Non-null assertions on env vars without validation
findings.description: Environment variables are accessed with non-null assertions (!) in multiple files. If these are not set, the application will crash at runtime rather than failing gracefully.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the existing `requireNodeEnvVar` function from `../../server/utils` to validate env vars at startup, or create a config initialization that validates all required env vars before the app starts.

findings.title: Magic number: Hardcoded test card number in pricing page
findings.description: The Stripe test card number '4242 4242 4242 4242 4242' is hardcoded in the pricing page UI.

locations.snippet: 4242 4242 4242 4242 4242

findings.suggested_fix: Move this to a constants file or configuration. While this is a well-known test value, keeping it separate makes it easier to update and document.

findings.title: Inconsistent error handling: Different patterns across payment webhooks
findings.description: Each payment provider webhook (Stripe, LemonSqueezy, Polar) uses slightly different patterns for error logging and response. This inconsistency makes maintenance harder.
findings.suggested_fix: Create a shared utility function for webhook error logging that all payment providers can use, ensuring consistent error handling behavior.

findings.title: Magic string: Hardcoded 'today' date in Google Analytics
findings.description: The string 'today' is used as a date parameter in the Google Analytics query. While it works, using dynamic dates would be more robust.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider adding a comment explaining that 'today' is a valid GA4 relative date, or create a constant for clarity.

findings.title: Code duplication: Payment plan card data repeated in component
findings.description: The `paymentPlanCards` object contains display data (name, price, features) that could be consolidated with the `paymentPlans` object in plans.ts
findings.suggested_fix: Consider consolidating plan metadata into a single source of truth, or at minimum ensure the `name` property in `paymentPlanCards` references the constant rather than duplicating `prettyPaymentPlanName()` calls.

findings.title: Dead code: Commented out logo reference in settings page
findings.description: In SettingsPage.tsx, there's a commented-out img tag for user photo that appears to be leftover from template creation.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the commented-out code or replace with actual image handling logic if user avatars are part of the feature set.

findings.title: Incomplete implementation: MessageButton has placeholder code
findings.description: The MessageButton component has a TODO comment indicating incomplete implementation for message notifications.

locations.snippet: {/* TODO: only animate if there are new messages */}

findings.suggested_fix: Implement the TODO by adding a prop or connecting to a real-time message count source to conditionally show the notification badge.

findings.title: Incomplete implementation: Settings form has placeholder submit
findings.description: The SettingsPage form has a TODO and alerts 'Not yet implemented' on submit.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the form submission logic or remove the form if not needed for the initial template release.

findings.title: Incomplete implementation: Messages page placeholder
findings.description: The AdminMessages page shows a placeholder 'under construction' message.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the messages feature or remove the route if not part of the planned functionality.

findings.title: Type safety: Generic type parameter uses any in throttle function
findings.description: The throttleWithTrailingInvocation function accepts `...args: any[]` which bypasses type safety for the throttled function.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a generic type parameter to preserve the function's parameter types: `export function throttleWithTrailingInvocation<T extends (...args: any[]) => any>(fn: T, ...)` and return `T & { cancel: () => void }`.

findings.title: Inconsistent constant patterns in pricing page
findings.description: The pricing page mixes inline constant definition (bestDealPaymentPlanId) with paymentPlanCards object. The constant could be in plans.ts for consistency.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider moving `bestDealPaymentPlanId` to plans.ts as a constant export if it's a fixed value, or make it configurable via environment variables.
